title: Check one imported observation
narration: In Imported observations, find x one equal to zero point five, input row eleven. Here, x is the liquid mole fraction and y is the vapor mole fraction. Under the ideal-vapor assumption, with negligible Poynting correction, y times total pressure equals x times gamma times saturation pressure. Rearranging gives gamma from the observed compositions and our property inputs. Notice that the table displays the natural logarithm of gamma. To compare with gamma itself, take the exponential of that table value. We will check this in Excel next.
on_screen: Lab 08 Imported observations: highlight input row 11 with x1=0.5, T=350 K, P=158.707198211 kPa and y1=0.704857144627. Emphasize the ln gamma column headings and the relationship gamma=EXP(ln gamma).

title: Verify the Excel formulas
narration: Switch to the workbook's Demo tab. Cells B twelve and B thirteen calculate saturation pressures of one hundred fifty and sixty kilopascals. B fourteen and B fifteen calculate gamma one and gamma two: approximately one point four nine one five four five, and one point five six one three seven seven. For component two, the formulas use one minus x one and one minus y one. B sixteen and B seventeen take the natural logarithms. Compare those with the Lab's log gamma values, allowing for displayed rounding. Agreement checks these calculations, not the property source independently.
on_screen: Excel Demo: show formulas and values in B12:B17. Highlight the observation links from VLE_data row 11 and show ln gamma1 approximately 0.399813 and ln gamma2 approximately 0.445568.

title: Save the validated baseline
narration: Return to Lab zero eight and save a baseline using Export complete study JSON. Give it a clear name, such as week zero two baseline. This file preserves the setup as well as recorded results; the observation CSV alone does not preserve the property settings. Keep Unmeasured endpoint intervals set to No extrapolation, no full-area verdict. Our observations do not cover the pure-component endpoints. Do not turn an incomplete composition interval into a full-area consistency claim. Keep that limitation with the baseline before fitting either model.
on_screen: Show Unmeasured endpoint intervals: No extrapolation · no full-area verdict. Select Export complete study JSON and display a distinct baseline filename, for example week02-baseline.json.

title: Fit and save one-parameter Margules
narration: Select Margules, one parameter, and then Fit selected model. Once fitting finishes, choose View: Pressure and vapor residuals. Here, the mean absolute pressure error is about one point one four one percent. The mean absolute vapor-composition error is about zero point six seven six percentage points. Record both metrics, inspect the residual pattern, and note any parameter-bound warning. Before changing models, export the complete study JSON and the fitted residuals CSV. Give both files Margules names so the next fit cannot be confused with this result.
on_screen: Show Margules · 1 parameter, Fit selected model, then View: Pressure and vapor residuals. Display full precision metrics approximately 1.14098% and 0.675676 percentage points. Show both exports with Margules filenames.

title: Fit NRTL with the same inputs
narration: Now choose N R T L, fixed alpha, and set alpha to zero point three. Leave the temperature-dependent parameter option unchecked. Keep the observations and property settings unchanged, then fit again. The pressure error is approximately one point one four times ten to the minus six percent, and the vapor error is about three point eight three times ten to the minus seven percentage points. These very small training errors are expected: N R T L generated the synthetic observations. This is model recovery, not evidence of universal superiority.
on_screen: Show NRTL · fixed alpha, alpha=0.3, and Fit tau_ij=c_ij+d_ij(350/T−1) unchecked. Fit and show the same residual view, approximately 1.14e-6% pressure error and 3.83e-7 percentage points vapor error.

title: Save NRTL results and read residual units
narration: Export the N R T L complete study JSON and fitted residuals CSV under separate, clearly named files. In the residuals CSV, y underscore error is the calculated minus observed vapor mole fraction. Multiply it by one hundred to express the difference in percentage points. The pressure underscore error underscore percent column is already a percentage. Do not multiply that column by one hundred again. Also distinguish individual signed residuals from the displayed mean absolute error, which averages their absolute values. Keep both model exports for comparison and recovery.
on_screen: Save distinct NRTL JSON and residual CSV filenames. Inspect exported headers y_error and pressure_error_percent, with note: y_error × 100 gives percentage points; pressure_error_percent is already percent.

title: Restore a saved study and recalculate
narration: Expand Study workspace, reopen and compare cases. Enter a label such as Restored Margules in Label for the next captured case. Use Load studies or a comparison JSON to select the saved Margules study. Then select its Restore button. Check the restored observations, units, property constants, and model controls. Loading first displays recorded results; it does not recalculate them. Restore loads the settings. Now select Validate and inspect data, followed by Fit selected model. Compare the fresh errors with the saved result to check that you recovered the same setup.
on_screen: Expand Study workspace · reopen and compare cases. Set case label, load the saved Margules JSON, select Restore [case label], inspect restored model and properties, then Validate & inspect data and Fit selected model.

title: State the finding and practice the workflow
narration: Finish with a finding, a number, and a limitation. For example, N R T L reproduces these synthetic training data more closely than Margules: compare the two pressure-error values you saved. But the generating model was N R T L, and training error alone does not establish thermodynamic consistency or prediction on new observations. Now allow about twenty minutes to repeat the full workflow yourself: export, import, verify one row, fit both models, save, and restore. Keep your files and corrections with the worksheet. This practice adds no new attendance task.
on_screen: Show a compact checklist: export CSV; import and validate; independently check row 11; fit and export both models; restore and refit; state finding, numerical evidence and limitation. Include: about 20 minutes of practice; no new attendance task.
pause_instruction: Pause and repeat the complete workflow in approximately 20 minutes. Keep your own exported files, numerical check, corrections and limitation statement with the original worksheet.
